nodes.subject: lithium-ion loaded terminal voltage
nodes.object: Open-circuit voltage, internal resistance and dynamic voltage drops; internal resistance rises significantly at low temperature. This is a generic model rather than a measurement of the worker's phone.

support_spans.exact_quote: a variable voltage source, representing the open-circuit voltage (OCV) of the cell, a resistor representing ohmic internal resistance of the cell and a set of resistor-capacitor (RC) parallels accounting for the dynamic voltage drops
The open-circuit voltage of a Li-ion cell (or battery) is its terminal voltage in equilibrium conditions, i.e. measured when no load current is applied and after a long rest period.
The internal resistance increases significantly at low temperatures.

accepted_phrases: A lithium-ion equivalent-circuit model separates open-circuit voltage from loaded terminal voltage, includes resistance and dynamic voltage drops, and says internal resistance rises significantly at low temperature. This makes a cold load-related voltage collapse plausible but does not measure the worker's phone or its exact state of charge.

nodes.subject: phone cutoff voltage
nodes.object: A shutdown at a prescribed terminal-voltage floor even while significant capacity remains. The page does not quantify this worker's hidden charge under cold conditions.

support_spans.exact_quote: Some electronic devices, such as cell phones, will automatically shut down when the cut-off voltage has been reached.
Devices that have too high cut-off voltages may stop operating while the battery still has significant capacity remaining.

accepted_phrases: Cell phones can automatically shut down when cutoff voltage is reached, and a device can stop while significant battery capacity remains. Combined with the low-temperature voltage model, this explains why displayed charge need not equal usable cold power, but it does not reveal an exact hidden percentage for this phone.

nodes.subject: thermal insulation
nodes.object: Heat transfer between objects at different temperature. It does not establish a phone-pouch duration without a test.

support_spans.exact_quote: Thermal insulation is the reduction of heat transfer (i.e., the transfer of thermal energy between objects of differing temperature) between objects in thermal contact or in range of radiative influence.
The act of insulation is accomplished by encasing an object in material with low thermal conductivity in high thickness.

accepted_phrases: Thermal insulation reduces heat transfer between objects at different temperatures, so carrying the phone and backup together in an insulated inner pouch can delay cooling. The generic page does not quantify how long a particular pouch keeps either battery within its operating range.

nodes.subject: generic battery-management controls
nodes.object: Voltage, temperature, state of charge, state of power, and operation outside a safe under-temperature boundary. Generic capability does not prove a particular product implementation.

support_spans.exact_quote: Temperature : average temperature, coolant intake temperature, coolant output temperature, or temperatures of individual cells
State of power (SoP), is the amount of power available for a defined time interval given the current power usage, temperature and other conditions
Under-temperature
Asking the devices to reduce or even stop using or charging the battery.

accepted_phrases: A battery management system may monitor voltage and temperature, calculate state of charge and state of power under current usage and temperature, and reduce or stop operation outside an under-temperature boundary. This generic capability does not prove how the worker's phone or any frozen product is configured.

nodes.subject: sudden cold shutdown mechanism
nodes.object: Low temperature raises internal resistance and loaded voltage drop, while cutoff and battery controls can stop a phone even when some chemical capacity remains. The chain is plausible and bounded, not a device diagnosis or exact hidden-charge measurement.

nodes.subject: winter field and power-bank experience
nodes.object: A really cold field anecdote supports carrying a warm backup and shows plausible charge counts, while other threads add portability and label-risk concerns. Missing temperature, model, capacity, energy and controlled-load data prevent transfer into a guaranteed product outcome.
